definition: Answering questions about a provided passage, testing whether a system actually understood the text.
details: Answering questions about a provided passage, testing whether a system actually understood the text. Benchmarks such as SQuAD and DROP drove much of the progress that led to modern LLMs.

explainer.lead: Reading comprehension tests whether a system can answer questions about a supplied passage. It matters as a direct check that a model is using the text rather than guessing.

tiers.eli5: Like a quiz where the answer is hidden in a short story you just read.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use these tasks to evaluate and fine-tune models on grounded answering. Pitfall: high benchmark scores can reflect pattern matching rather than genuine understanding.
tiers.paperLevel: Given a passage P and a question Q, produce an answer A derived from P, often scored by exact match or F1 against reference answers. Benchmarks such as SQuAD and DROP drove progress toward modern LLMs; scores measure task performance, not comprehension in a general sense.

explainer.example: Given a paragraph about a city's population and a question about its size, the system extracts the stated figure.
